clue.text: Better from Maesteg, right?

indicators.note: the letters come from the place name reshaped, so the town is rearranged rather than taken as is

explanation.surface: A gambler hailing from the Welsh town of Maesteg, the clue asks.
explanation.walkthrough: Maesteg is a town in South Wales; 'from' signals that its letters are rearranged to MAESTEG then R is added. 'Better' is not the comparative of good but one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler who places wagers is literally someone who bets.

clue.text: Indistinct speech coming from bachelor with a follower in the wind

indicators.note: the two letters sit inside the word for a strong wind, so 'in' marks the container

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree
the letter that follows A in the alphabet is B

explanation.surface: Muffled talk from a single man and his companion lost in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a follower' is the letter that follows A, namely B.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk rapidly and unintelligibly is to jabber or babble.

clue.text: This Finn could knock out a mouse

definitions.meaning: a ... Finn is a drugged drink that renders the drinker unconscious

explanation.surface: A Finnish person strong enough to flatten a small rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finn' looks like a Finnish person, but it completes the phrase Mickey Finn, a spiked drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The first half of the phrase naming a knockout drink, and the first name of the Disney cartoon rodent.

clue.text: Imagined having had some food, so upset inside

indicators.note: the reversed short word goes within the word for having eaten, as 'inside' says

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper, so supped means had some food

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word so is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone thinking they ate, with a stomach so upset.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns its word upside down, so it reads backwards; 'having' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have supposed something is to have assumed or believed it in the mind.

clue.text: Eat out in style, though it stretches resources

indicators.note: the answer lies within the letters of the word stretches, so 'in' points at that word

explanation.surface: Dining lavishly at a restaurant, though it strains the budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' looks like dining at a restaurant, but it means to corrode, as acid does a plate; the letters sit in the middle of 'stretches'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid corroding a metal plate to make an engraving is the process meant.

clue.text: Be right on the heels of the big man

indicators.note: following close behind something, so these pieces come after the word for big

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for big

explanation.surface: Stay close behind the boss, a piece of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big man' tempts as the definition, but 'big' is clothing's outsize label and 'man' alone defines; 'on the heels of' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Osbert is a male first name, as borne by the writer Osbert Sitwell.

clue.text: Way to go round on foot

definitions.text: Way to go round on foot

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to roll is to turn over and over, going round

explanation.surface: A method of travelling around by walking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a leisurely walk while also giving ST and ROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely walk is a gentle way of getting about by foot.

clue.text: A simple brain makes for a clear conscience

parts.note: easy means simple, not difficult
the mind is the brain's thinking faculty

explanation.surface: Being simple-minded leaves one free of guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Having nothing to feel guilty about leaves one untroubled and at peace.

clue.text: Drawing an old engine

definitions.meaning: the act of pulling a load along a surface
a steam-powered road locomotive of the nineteenth century, named for this word

explanation.surface: A sketch of a vintage locomotive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests a picture, but it means pulling.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling power is the first sense; the second completes the name of a steam road locomotive.

clue.text: Support scouting group by providing hiking kit

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a Cub Scout unit is called a pack

explanation.surface: Sponsoring the local Scouts by supplying their camping equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack carried by walkers holds their gear.

clue.text: Big run on a famous Swiss bank

definitions.text: Big run on a famous Swiss bank

parts.words: Big run on a famous Swiss bank
parts.note: reads like a financial panic at a Zurich bank, but means a celebrated toboggan course with banked bends at St Moritz

explanation.surface: A rush of savers withdrawing money from a well-known Swiss bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' and 'bank' suggest finance; the run is a toboggan course and the bank is its snow-banked curve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cresta Run at St Moritz is the world-famous Swiss tobogganing course.

clue.text: Man leaves a German to enter cathedral city with enthusiasm

indicators.note: the short pieces go into the city name, entering it

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

indicators.note: the word man departs from the word German, leaving its first three letters

parts.note: the nationality word from which a part is removed
the letters removed from the word German

explanation.surface: A man exits while a German heads into an English cathedral town keenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' reads as a person but is the letters removed by 'leaves'; Ely is a small cathedral city near Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something keenly and impatiently is acting with eagerness.

clue.text: Utter base calumny then hide

parts.note: a lie is a base, slanderous falsehood
cattle low, uttering their moo

explanation.surface: Spread vile slander, then go into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' is not an adjective here but a verb: to low is what cattle do when they moo.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep out of sight and avoid attention is to stay hidden.

clue.text: It could be set at your place, or mine

definitions.text: It could be set at your place, or mine

parts.words: It could be set at your place, or mine
parts.note: your place at a dinner table, where cutlery and a protective square are laid

explanation.surface: Something that might be laid at your home or at mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your place' sounds like your home, but it is your place setting at the dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat-resistant pad laid beneath a plate at each diner's setting.

clue.text: Once more a righteous man is in opposition

parts.note: again means once more
a saint, abbreviated ST, is a righteous person

explanation.surface: Again a virtuous man finds himself opposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something is standing contrary to it.

clue.text: Hounds chasing black birds

indicators.note: the birds follow behind the letter for black, as a chaser comes after

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
eagles are large birds of prey

explanation.surface: Hunting dogs pursuing dark-coloured birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' puts EAGLES after B.
explanation.definitionFit: Small scent-hunting dogs used for hare-hunting are a kind of hound.

clue.text: A French firm is remarkable in Scotland

parts.note: un is the French for a
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A French company is noteworthy north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Unco is a Scots word meaning remarkable or very.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means strange or extraordinary.

clue.text: Support also arranged for the suggested plan

parts.note: a prop supports something

indicators.note: the letters of also are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Backing was also organised for the proposed scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles the letters of 'also'; 'for the' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan put forward for consideration is an offered scheme.

clue.text: Weed killer some spread around water

indicators.note: a portion is spread round the water word, so it encloses it

parts.note: part means some of something
aqua is Latin for water

explanation.surface: A herbicide, some of it sprinkled about the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread around' wraps the portion round the Latin water word; aqua for water is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxic herbicide used to destroy unwanted plants.

clue.text: The writer going around to match a colour

indicators.note: the writer's tool encloses the other word, going round it

parts.note: a pen is what a writer writes with
to agree is to match or correspond

explanation.surface: An author travelling about to find a matching shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' suggests a person, but it is the tool; 'going around' wraps it round the word for match.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright yellowish-green shade like fresh peas.

clue.text: See what's written concerning publicity

parts.note: re means concerning, about
an ad is an advertisement, publicity

explanation.surface: Look at the text about advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at and taking in text on a page is what this verb means.

clue.text: Silly man sometimes?

parts.note: silly is not foolish here but a cricket term for close-in positions such as silly point

explanation.surface: A foolish fellow now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, silly mid-on and silly point are close catching positions taken by a player of the batting side's opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer stationed at silly point or silly mid-off is one of the team's catchers.

clue.text: Game is arranged for such pictures

indicators.note: the letters of game and is are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A game that is laid out to produce photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles GAMEIS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Representations or likenesses, such as photographs.

clue.text: Climbed up in an hierarchical system

definitions.meaning: ascended, as up a cliff or ladder
graded in ranked steps or levels

explanation.surface: Rose through the ranks of an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascending a wall or mountain is one sense; arranged in graduated levels on a ladder of grades is the other.

clue.text: It modifies the blood and may be vent

definitions.meaning: an abdominal organ that filters and processes blood cells
bad temper, which is often said to be vented

explanation.surface: Something that alters blood and might be let out.
explanation.walkthrough: To vent one's spleen is an idiom for giving vent to anger.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdominal organ filtering blood is one sense; the anger one vents in the idiom is the other.

clue.text: Fortune-teller accepts old money for David

indicators.note: the palm reader takes in the coin abbreviation, accepting it inside

parts.note: a palmist tells fortunes by reading palms
S is the abbreviation for a shilling, pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant takes payment in pre-decimal coins from a client called David.
explanation.walkthrough: King David is traditionally credited with composing the Psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally the author of the biblical Psalms.

clue.text: Trophy for champion layer?

parts.note: the prize cup for the best egg-laying hen, which humorously is a small cup for a boiled egg

explanation.surface: A prize awarded to the best bricklayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a bricklayer, but it is a hen that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup holding a boiled egg upright at breakfast.

clue.text: A lover of attractive women-but no ties!

indicators.note: no means without, so the word ties is dropped from the women

parts.note: beauties are attractive women
the letters removed from the end

explanation.surface: A ladies' man with no commitments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes TIES from BEAUTIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend or admirer is an old-fashioned sweetheart.

clue.text: Smear some of this mud generally in

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is taken, so some of them gives the answer

explanation.surface: Applying some of this mud widely.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'this', 'mud' and 'generally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirty mark or streak is a smudge.

clue.text: A stirring call for military personnel

definitions.text: A stirring call for military personnel

parts.words: A stirring call for military personnel
parts.note: stirring means rousing from sleep rather than inspiring, so the bugle call that wakes troops

explanation.surface: An inspiring summons to the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' suggests rousing patriotism; it means waking up.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle signal sounded at dawn to wake soldiers.

clue.text: News of the overseas cricket match

parts.note: la is the French for the
a test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Tidings of a cricket game played abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match lasting up to five days.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent news is the newest information.

clue.text: In the Piedmontese capital Kelly retired

indicators.note: the outlaw's name goes in the city name

parts.note: Turin is the capital of Piedmont in Italy
Ned Kelly was a famous Australian outlaw

explanation.surface: Someone named Kelly withdrew in the capital of Piedmont.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly was a nineteenth-century Australian bushranger; 'In' at the start signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to bed for the night is the idiomatic sense of retiring.
